Piṇḍapitṛyajña
(‘sacrifice to the manes by offering rice balls’)
------------------------------------------
Performance of the śrāddhas or obse-quial rites in honour of the dead ancestors—generally of three generations—is an ancient custom. It has its origin in such Vedic rites such as the पिण्डपितृयज्ञ.
This rite is generally performed one day prior to the Darśa sacrifice by an आहिताग्नि (one who keeps the Vedic fires duly established). The procedure is similar to that of the पार्वणश्राद्ध. (See ŚRĀDDHA for details.)
Three piṇḍas (rice-balls) have to be offered in the afternoon to the पितृस् or forefathers. The rice has to be cooked over दक्षिणाग्नि (See DAKṢIṆĀGNI.) and sprinkled with आज्य or ghee. At the time of offering the piṇḍas the performer has to wear his यज्ञोपवीत in the प्राचीनावीत form, i.e., on the right shoulder, hanging on the left side, below the left arm. (See NIVĪTA.)
Offerings are to be made in the दक्षिणाग्नि to gods and अग्नि (as kavya-वाहन, carrier of offerings) first.
Reception rites to the पितृस्, prayers to them followed by नमस्कार or obeisance, are some of the other rites.
